questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

The counselor gave very good advice to the students.

options.text: Very good advice was given to the students by the counselor.
Very good advice is given to the students by the counselor.
Very good advice to the students has been given by the counselor.
Very good advice to the students had been given by the counselor.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Very good advice was given to the students by the counselor**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the active voice and it is in the past simple tense.
 
• When we convert this sentence into a passive voice, the subject ''The counselor'' of the active voice becomes the object, the object ''very good advice'' becomes the subject.
 
• The active format "V2 (gave)" should be converted into the passive format "was + V3 (given)".
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the past simple tense.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Verbs of passive format have a different set of tenses (*V3 - Past participle or Third form of the Verb) as given below in the table:

• Active Voice में , एक वाक्य विषय पर जोर देता है, एक क्रिया करता है।
 
• Passive Voice में , एक वाक्य वाक्य की क्रिया या वस्तु पर जोर देता है।
 
• दिया गया वाक्य active voice में है और यह past simple tense में है।
 
• जब हम इस वाक्य को passive voice में बदलते हैं, तो active voice का subject 'The counselor', object बन जाता है और object 'very good advice', subject बन जाता है।
 
• Active format "V2 (gave)" को passive format "was + V3 (given)" में परिवर्तित किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• यह past simple tense के लिए active and passive voice rule है।

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.**

These days, wherever district courts are functioning, __hearings is limit__ to urgent matters.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**hearings are limited**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the underlined segment, the use of the singular form of the verb 'is' and the base form of the verb 'limit' is incorrect.
 
• The **subject 'hearings'** in the underlined segment is **a plural subject** and it **will take a plural verb**.
 
• Therefore, the plural form of the verb 'are' should be used in place of the singular form of the verb 'is'.
 
• Also, the **given sentence is a passive voice in the present simple tense**.
 
• In the **present simple**, the **passive format is**: **am/is/are + past participle (3rd form of the verb)**.
 
• Therefore, the past participle form of the verb 'limited' should be used in place of the base form of the verb 'limit'.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct Sentence: *These days, wherever district courts are functioning, **hearings are limited** to urgent matters*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

 
• रेखांकित खण्ड में **क्रिया 'is' के एकवचन रूप** का प्रयोग तथा **क्रिया '**limit**' के मूल रूप का प्रयोग गलत है**।
 
• रेखांकित खंड में subject 'hearings' एक **बहुवचन subject है** और **यह एक बहुवचन क्रिया लेगा**।
 
• इसलिए **क्रिया के एकवचन रूप** 'is' के स्थान पर क्रिया के **बहुवचन रूप** 'are' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• साथ ही, **दिया गया वाक्य वर्तमान सरल काल में** एक passive voice है।
 
• **वर्तमान सरल में, passive प्रारूप** है: **am/is/are + past participle (क्रिया का तीसरा रूप)**।
 
• इसलिए base form of the verb 'limit' के स्थान पर past participle form of the verb 'limited' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।

 

अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।

सही वाक्य: *These days, wherever district courts are functioning, hearings are limited to urgent matters*.

questions.question:
**Directions: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, select the one that gives their correct order.**

A. It is only after sunset that he satisfies his hunger and quenches his thirst.

B. In this way, by practicing self-restraint for one month in a year, he is able to lead a life of self-discipline in all matters for the rest of the year.

C. During the month of Ramzan, the believer abstains from food and drink in the daytime of his own free will.

D. Fasting is an exercise in self-discipline and is good for everyone.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'DCAB.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence 'D' is independent of any other sentence as it is giving general information about "Fasting". Hence, 'D' is the first part.
 
• Sentence C will come after D as it is giving information about what happens during Ramzan fasting (the believer abstains from food and drink in the daytime of his own free will).
 
• Sentence A will come after C as it is giving information about when the believer breaks his fast (only after sunset).
 
• The sentence 'B' is the concluding part as it is giving information about how the believer is able **to lead a life of self-discipline in all matters for the rest of the year** (by practicing self-restraint or fasting for one month in a year).

 

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences__: *Fasting is an exercise in self-discipline and is good for everyone. During the month of Ramzan, the believer abstains from food and drink in the daytime of his own free will. It is only after sunset that he satisfies his hunger and quenches his thirst. In this way, by practicing self-restraint for one month in a year, he is able to lead a life of self-discipline in all matters for the rest of the year.*

__
 
• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles__:

 __
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
 
• Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
 
• Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

 
• वाक्य '**D**' किसी अन्य वाक्य से स्वतंत्र है क्योंकि यह "**उपवास**" के बारे में सामान्य जानकारी दे रहा है। अतः '**D**' पहला भाग है।
 
• वाक्य C, D के बाद आएगा क्योंकि यह इस बारे में जानकारी दे रहा है कि रमजान के उपवास के दौरान क्या होता है (आस्तिक अपनी मर्जी से दिन में खाने-पीने से परहेज करता है)।
 
• वाक्य A, C के बाद आएगा क्योंकि यह इस बारे में जानकारी दे रहा है कि आस्तिक कब अपना उपवास तोड़ता है (केवल सूर्यास्त के बाद)।
 
• वाक्य 'B' समापन भाग है क्योंकि यह इस बारे में जानकारी दे रहा है कि आस्तिक कैसे शेष वर्ष के लिए सभी मामलों में आत्म-अनुशासन का जीवन जीने में सक्षम है (साल में एक महीने के लिए आत्म-संयम या उपवास का अभ्यास करके)।

The manager said that Rahul does not wants to go to Mumbai for the new project.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The phrase **"does not wants"** is grammatically incorrect because the auxiliary verb **"does"** requires the base form of the main verb.
 
• The correct form should be **"does not want"**, not **"does not wants"**.
 
• This is a rule in English grammar where auxiliary verbs like **"do/does"** are followed by the base form of the verb (without adding -s).

Correct sentence: *The manager said that Rahul does not want to go to Mumbai for the new project.*

• **Rule for Auxiliary Verbs:**

 
 
• When using auxiliary verbs like **"do/does"** in negative sentences, always use the base form of the main verb.
 
• Example: **She does not like chocolate.** (Correct) vs. **She does not likes chocolate.** (Incorrect).
 
 
 
• **Common Auxiliary Verbs:**
 
 
• **Do/Does:** Used for present tense.
 
• **Did:** Used for past tense.
 
• Always followed by the base verb.
